key_insight: LLM-based agents can be assembled into geographically grounded synthetic populations that partially reproduce real-world public health behavior at the community level.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help researchers simulate population responses to screening and other interventions before real-world deployment, but it is not yet reliable enough to replace observed data.
method: Built LLMPopSim using U.S. Census and CDC data to create AI agents representing local populations.
Trained the framework on Hawaii 2018 data and tested temporal/geographic transfer on held-out 2022 cohorts from Hawaii and New York State.
Evaluated simulated colorectal cancer screening and mammography against observed ZCTA-level prevalence.
evidence_signal: Across four state-outcome tests, mean absolute error was 3.5-15.0 percentage points and correlations with observed ZCTA-level prevalence ranged from 0.26 to 0.69.
watch_item: Performance was least accurate in lower-prevalence communities and showed calibration and subgroup-fidelity gaps, so implementation requires careful validation.
paper_title: Evaluating agentic simulation for local public health estimation
